content: a16z's David George and Gavin Baker discuss why AI demand may be underestimated and compute supply is struggling to keep pace. They explore how frontier labs, open-source models, applications, clouds, and NVIDIA could all capture value as adoption expands. Topics include infrastructure economics, fast payback periods on compute investments, risks of AI shortage versus bubble, data center backlash, orbital compute, multi-model architectures, and NVIDIA's central role in the supply chain. title: 对AI需求、基建与增长的思考
content: AI demand differs from past tech cycles: internet growth depended solely on user penetration, while AI demand depends on both penetration and per-user token consumption, which has only begun growing. Data center investments show strong unit economics with ~60% capital returns and drive regional economic revitalization through jobs and infrastructure. Enterprise AI revenue is increasingly driven by generalized coding tasks across professions, not just software developers. Open-source models remain small due to high compute barriers, while closed-source providers use tiered pricing strategies. AI's expansion into productive and decision-making workflows suggests a longer infrastructure cycle than markets currently assume.
